name: Bartok
description: Bartok is a high-speed shedding game belonging to the Crazy Eights family, famous for its 'Meta-Game' mechanic. While it begins as a simple match-suit-or-rank contest, the winner of each round earns the right to add a new permanent rule to the game. These rules accumulate across rounds, turning a simple children's game into a complex, rule-heavy nightmare of memory and trap-setting. Unlike its more secretive cousin 'Mao', the new rules in Bartok are explicitly announced, but the sheer volume of stacking triggers quickly leads to chaos and penalties.

content.text: Bartok is a high-speed shedding game belonging to the Crazy Eights family, famous for its 'Meta-Game' mechanic. While it begins as a simple match-suit-or-rank contest, the winner of each round earns the right to add a new permanent rule to the game. These rules accumulate across rounds, turning a simple children's game into a complex, rule-heavy nightmare of memory and trap-setting. Unlike its more secretive cousin 'Mao', the new rules in Bartok are explicitly announced, but the sheer volume of stacking triggers quickly leads to chaos and penalties.

Originating in Australia in the mid-20th century as a social variant of 'Eights' or 'Uno'. It was designed to maintain interest over long sessions by allowing the game to evolve, becoming more difficult as the night progressed.
One standard 52-card deck for 2-5 players. Two decks for 6 or more.
Standard pack, score sheet, and a pen/paper to record the new rules.
Dealer (rotating) deals 7 cards to each player. The next card is turned face up to start the discard pile; the remainder is the draw pile.

items.text: Secret Bartok: Only the rule-maker knows the new rule. Others must deduce it through penalty cards (Mao-style).
Progressive Bartok: Rules only last for 3 rounds then expire, preventing the 'rule-clog' of late games.
